items.name: N+1 on the conversation list + a dropped/retuned needed index
items.compound_note: Both halves (a N+1 and b missing index) planted per the catalog #7 recipe.

halves.name: N+1 message count on the conversation list
halves.exact_change: `pluralize(conversation.messages_count, "message")` -> `pluralize(conversation.messages.count, "message")`. The model displays the per-conversation message count via the `messages_count` counter_cache COLUMN (Message belongs_to :conversation, counter_cache: true -> zero per-row queries). The edit replaces the cached column read with `conversation.messages.count`, firing `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = ?` once PER conversation rendered.
halves.routed_path_evidence: GET / and GET /conversations -> ConversationsController#index -> `@conversations = current_user.conversations.recent.limit(100)` -> renders conversations/_sidebar (and the mobile list) which renders the `conversations/conversation` partial as a COLLECTION -> 1+N (up to 100 extra COUNT queries). Also rendered on GET /conversations/:id (show renders the sidebar). routes.rb:9 resources :conversations.
halves.live_verify: ruby -c n/a (ERB). grep app/views/conversations/_conversation.html.erb:9 => `conversation.messages.count`. N+1 is LIVE on the index/sidebar collection render; value identical (counter_cache == COUNT), so happy-path assertions stay green. The ONLY query-count guard in the suite is admin_report_test.rb:163 `assert_queries_count(1)`, which exercises the AdminReport service (user_breakdown), NOT this view -> unaffected. conversations#index/show have no query-count assertion. chat_flow_test.rb:19 `assert_selector "aside", text: "2 messages"` stays green (same number).
halves.adaptation: The model's admin reports listing (AdminReport#user_breakdown) is query-count-GUARDED (admin_report_test.rb:163), so an N+1 there would redden the suite (gate 3). Per the minimax_m3_1_flash / deepseek_v4_1_flash precedent, the N+1 is planted on the model's real UNGUARDED listing — the conversation list on the app's main page. Faithful 'drop the preloaded/cached grouped count -> per-row .count' regression; here the preload is a counter_cache column rather than a controller-side grouped query, so the equivalent change is column-read -> association .count. Same class (N+1), same Med 2.

halves.name: needed activity-rollup index dropped and replaced by a non-serving composite
halves.exact_change: New migration `remove_index :messages, :created_at` + `add_index :messages, [:role, :created_at]`. schema.rb version 2026_10_20_120000 -> 2026_10_20_120001; messages block's `t.index ["created_at"], name: "index_messages_on_created_at"` replaced by `t.index ["role", "created_at"], name: "index_messages_on_role_and_created_at"`.
halves.routed_path_evidence: The dropped bare-created_at index backed AdminReport#activity (app/services/admin_report.rb:111 `Message.where(created_at: start_time..)` grouped by DATE(created_at), NO role predicate), rendered on GET /admin, /admin/dashboard, /admin/reports (dashboard#index). A [role, created_at] composite (leading column role) cannot serve a pure created_at range/group scan -> the daily message activity bucket now does a full-table scan.
halves.live_verify: ruby -c OK on migration and schema.rb. grep -c index_messages_on_created_at db/schema.rb => 0; index_messages_on_role_and_created_at => 1; control indexes index_conversations_on_created_at => 1 and index_users_on_created_at => 1 (untouched). No test asserts index presence -> suite green; no boot break. Fix = restore index_messages_on_created_at (corrective migration + schema.rb).
halves.adaptation: Identical to the minimax_m3_1_flash / deepseek_v4_1_flash #7b recipe (drop the sprint-4 messages.created_at index backing the activity rollup; add a plausible-but-false [:role, :created_at] composite; schema synced).

items.name: silently wrong aggregate — admins total counts only ACTIVE admins
items.exact_change: `(SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN admin THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM users) AS admins_count` -> `(SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN admin AND active THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM users) AS admins_count`. The 'Total admins' figure now excludes any administrator who has been deactivated (deactivate! sets active=false but KEEPS the admin role), so the dashboard under-reports the admin headcount. Ground truth (count of admins regardless of active) != the reported number whenever a deactivated admin exists.
items.routed_path_evidence: Rendered on the dashboard Admins card: app/views/admin/dashboard/index.html.erb:31 `<%= number_with_delimiter(@totals.admins) %> admins`, via Admin::DashboardController#index (GET /admin, /admin/dashboard, /admin/reports).
items.live_verify: ruby -c OK. grep app/services/admin_report.rb:11 => `CASE WHEN admin AND active`. Green-but-wrong: the sole pins are admin_report_test.rb:25 `assert_equal 1, totals.admins` and dashboard_controller_test.rb:51 `assert_select "#total-admins", text: "1"` — in both the only admin fixture is ACTIVE (and in the controller test the deactivated user @inactive is a non-admin), so the figure stays 1 and the suite passes. No test deactivates an admin and then checks totals.admins, so the undercount never surfaces in CI.
items.adaptation: Same narrowing as the minimax_m3_1_flash / deepseek_v4_1_flash / qwen38strix #8 (admin count -> active-admin count). Applied to this model's raw-SQL TOTALS query (equivalent of their `User.admin.count -> User.admin.active.count`).

items.name: delete a needed file — wired Stimulus controller removed
items.exact_change: Deleted the entire chat Stimulus controller. It is still WIRED by the views: conversations/show.html.erb:6 `data-controller="chat"` + :22/:28/:34 `data-action="chat#usePrompt"`, and messages/_composer.html.erb:4 `turbo:submit-start->chat#submitting turbo:submit-end->chat#submitted`, :13 `chat_target: "input"`, :14 `input->chat#autogrow keydown->chat#keydown`, plus the submit button `data-chat-target="submit"`. controllers/index.js uses `eagerLoadControllersFrom("controllers", ...)` (importmap.rb `pin_all_from app/javascript/controllers`), so the missing file raises NO JS/boot error — the controller just never registers.
items.routed_path_evidence: Loaded on GET /conversations/:id (the chat workspace) and in the composer rendered there and on message create (create.turbo_stream.erb:23). Silently lost behaviors: Enter-to-send (ADVERTISED in the composer footer :36 'Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line'), submit busy/disabled state, textarea autogrow, auto-scroll-to-bottom on new messages (MutationObserver), and click-a-suggestion-to-fill (usePrompt).
items.live_verify: ls app/javascript/controllers/ => application.js, flash_controller.js, index.js (chat_controller.js gone). grep -rn 'chat_controller' app/ config/ test/ => none (never referenced by filename; eager-loaded by glob, so no stale import). git show 979840f --stat => 1 file deleted, 77 deletions. Suite stays GREEN: chat_flow_test.rb submits via `fill_in` + `click_button "Send"` (never Enter, never a prompt suggestion) and all its assertions are server/Turbo-driven — messages append via create.turbo_stream.erb, the input is cleared SERVER-SIDE (create.turbo_stream.erb:23 re-renders #composer with Message.new, so `assert_equal "", find_field("message_content").value` holds without the controller), the header/sidebar/message-count come from Turbo-stream re-renders, and Capybara visibility is unaffected by scroll position. No test asserts Enter-to-send, busy-state, autogrow, auto-scroll, or usePrompt. Fix = `git restore` the file (NOT recreate).
items.adaptation: Direct analog of the minimax_m3_1_flash #9 (delete a wired-but-unexercised Stimulus controller). This model folded the composer form-submit UX (Enter-to-send + busy-state + autofocus) that peers carried in a separate message_composer/message_form controller INTO chat_controller.js; that controller's unique behaviors are all unexercised by the suite, making it the faithful same-class, same-severity target. (flash_controller.js was the weaker alternative analog and was NOT chosen.)
